title: Mathematics for Machine Learning
instructions: Ten questions. Some have more than one correct answer; select every correct option. Exact match earns one point. Answers are revealed only after submission in the interface.

questions.prompt: Two measurements, height and reflectance, are used to predict whether an object belongs to class A or B. Which values are the input features?
options: The measured height and reflectance
The classes A and B
The number of correct predictions
The final score of the classifier
questions.explanation: Features are the measured input properties. A/B is the target label.

questions.prompt: A dataset contains measurements but no predefined categories. We want to discover groups of similar records. Which task fits?
options: Supervised classification
Unsupervised clustering
Numerical regression with given targets
Evaluation on a labelled test set
questions.explanation: Clustering groups observations without supplied class labels.

questions.prompt: What is the arithmetic mean of the numbers 2, 4, 6 and 8?
questions.explanation: The sum is 20; dividing by four gives 5.

questions.prompt: What is the median of the sorted observations 2, 3, 4, 20, 21?
questions.explanation: There are five values, so the median is the central (third) value: 4.

questions.prompt: In a labelled dataset, three of four examples have class 'yes'. What fraction of the records are 'yes'?
questions.explanation: Three yes labels out of four examples give 3/4 = 0.75.

questions.prompt: What is the binary Shannon entropy (in bits) when two classes each have probability 1/2?
A group contains 12 examples and every label is 'A'. What is its class entropy?
options: 0 bits
0.5 bits
1 bit
12 bits
questions.explanation: A pure class distribution has zero uncertainty about the class label; entropy is 0.

questions.prompt: A collected table contains a missing temperature value. What is the most defensible first step?
options: Replace it with zero without checking the meaning
Delete the complete dataset
Inspect how missing values are encoded and decide a handling rule
Assume it equals the largest recorded temperature
questions.explanation: Missing values must be identified and handled deliberately, with the rule documented.

questions.prompt: Select ALL appropriate practices before sharing a small labelled classroom dataset.
options: Remove direct personal identifiers if the data are shared
Inspect missing and inconsistent values
Assume the collected examples represent every student
Change uncertain labels to positive without checking
questions.explanation: Privacy-aware sharing and data-quality checks are appropriate. Representativeness and labels need evidence, not assumptions.

questions.prompt: Select ALL actions that make comparisons between two groups' average sensor readings more meaningful.
options: Compare values measured in the same units
Report the number of observations in each group
Treat every missing measurement as exactly zero without justification
Ignore that one group uses centimetres and the other uses metres
questions.explanation: Matching units and reporting sample sizes help interpret averages. Missingness and incompatible units cannot safely be ignored.
